1.explanation:
• MultiSelect.js: the main component needs a new readOnly: PropTypes.bool entry, and its internal event handlers (e.g. onChange wrapper) must bail out or suppress interactions when readOnly is true. 
• MultiSelectPropTypes.js: include readOnly in the component’s prop-type definitions so it’s documented and type-checked. 
• MultiSelect.stories.js: expose the readOnly prop in argTypes and add a default story demonstrating the read-only state for easy copy-and-paste. 
• MultiSelect-test.js: add RTL tests to verify that when readOnly=true, the dropdown does not open, items cannot be toggled, and the custom read-only class is rendered on the root element.
1.bug_scenario: The two design-system reference diagrams illustrate a “read-only” variant of the MultiSelect control: it should render with the same spacing, tag look, and placeholder text, but not respond to user interactions (no opening the list, no toggling tags) while still showing selected items styled like tags with the custom “read-only” class. A new readOnly prop must be added to the React MultiSelect component, with associated styles, storybook knobs, and tests to validate the non-interactive read-only state.

2.explanation: All of the read-only behavior must be implemented inside the MultiSelect component in MultiSelect.js. The component’s prop‐type declarations (MultiSelect.propTypes) need a new Boolean readOnly entry, and the internal stateReducer (the Downshift stateReducer function) must short-circuit any open/close or selection changes when readOnly is true. MultiSelect.js is where the handlers for opening the menu, toggling items, and removing tags live, so it must be updated to disable those actions in read-only mode. Finally, the PropTypes file must export the new readOnly property so the component’s API and documentation include the prop.
2.bug_scenario: The goal is to add a read‐only mode to the MultiSelect component so that, when the new readOnly prop is true, the control renders in a non-interactive style (matches the Carbon design spec shown in the screenshots), the dropdown cannot be opened or modified, and any selected tags cannot be removed. In the first image we see the normal editable multi-select. In the second image we see the intended read-only appearance: the input and dropdown arrow remain visible but do not respond to hover/focus/click, and the tags are displayed but their “X” removal controls are not interactive.
